title: Per-org capacity: concurrency caps with backlog and fair share, per-class rate limits and plan-aware quotas
summary: Add a per-org concurrency cap with a bounded backlog and fair-share priority inside the existing Postgres queue (Firecrawl pattern: over-limit work waits with an expiry, 429 only when the backlog is full), per-endpoint-class rate limits on the gateway browser, scrape and search routes, and plan-keyed limits read from Control Plane entitlements via claims (no cross-plane DB reads).
whyItMatters: With a two-session lease pool and no per-org caps, one tenant can starve all others; the browser, search and ingestion gateway routes have no rate limiting (SRC per baseline). Plan-scaled limits are table-stakes for web platforms (Firecrawl SRC, Apify DOC).

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (tenant backlog with expiry, in-flight priority penalty, 429 only on backlog overflow)
others: Firecrawl (SRC)
Firecrawl (per-endpoint base limits times a plan multiplier, with org override)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources; differentiator (Apify documents plan concurrency limits but not this mechanism) || 1 of 4 sources (Firecrawl); unique as a documented design || 2 of 4 sources (both crawl platforms); common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Sync path: a per-tenant lease semaphore (holders with TTL, heartbeated) waits up to 2/3 of the request timeout with jittered backoff. Async path: if active(org) >= limit, insert into backlog(org, job, times_out_at) instead of the queue; when a job finishes, promote the oldest backlog entry respecting per-crawl max concurrency; a reaper expires backlog rows (max 48 h). Backlog capacity = clamp(limit x 2000, 50k, 2M); overflow returns 429 naming the limit. Fair share: priority stays at base until in_flight(org, 60 s window) exceeds a bucket limit, then base + ceil((count - bucketLimit) x planModifier). || Merged items add: A Redis limiter keyed by (org, endpoint class). Limit = base[class] x plan multiplier, with per-org overrides. Cheap status polling has a high limit and browser sessions a low one. The limiter fails open if the entitlement lookup is down, and returns 429 with Retry-After. || BASE_RATE_LIMITS per endpoint class (scrape 10, map 10, crawl 2, search 10, extract 2, browser 2, status 500 per minute) multiplied by a plan multiplier (1, 10, 50, 500), with per-org overrides per mode; a token-bucket limiter keyed by (org, mode); priority tier derived from the same multiplier. Quotas are counted on create (schedules, webhooks) and rejected with a typed error.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: Only a read-only team-concurrency view exists; no backlog or fairness; per-org vector budget only; plan-aware quotas unverified (light grep; NV).

approachOriginal: Ingestion Plane queue admission + Frontend gateway rate_limit.rs classes + Control Plane entitlement keys. Shares the admission code with F-t2-006. || Source detail: [R-t2-05-05] Ingestion Plane enforces, Control Plane owns the numbers. Quarry reads the org's concurrency limit from the verified principal or an entitlement call, counts active rows per org in the same Postgres queue (no second store), adds an org_backlog table promoted on completion, applies an in-flight priority penalty in the claim ORDER BY (postgres_queue.rs), and returns a typed 429 with Retry-After. Count agent browser leases against the same org budget or a sibling cap so agent fleets cannot bypass it (INF). Frontend: show queue position via the existing team queue-status route. First make the durable frontier the only production crawl path (hardening of the existing queue: remove the in-workflow slice fallback, add a stall counter with max-stall fail-out). || [R-t2-04-11] Frontend Plane gateway: replace the single DEFAULT_RPM bucket lookup with a class-aware limiter (class derived from route, key = org, base limits multiplied by Control Plane plan entitlements, separate interactive and agent classes so human browsing is not throttled by agents). Ingestion Plane: per-org permit accounting in the lease pool (guaranteed minimum plus burst) and a coarse per-org backstop in quarry-edge that returns the existing RATE_LIMITED envelope with retry_after_seconds. || [R-t2-05-10] Control Plane owns the multiplier and quota numbers and exposes them in the principal or entitlement claims. Quarry edge applies a token bucket per (org, endpoint class: scrape, map, crawl, search, extract, browser, status) with Retry-After, and checks quota counts when creating schedules and webhooks. Gateway keeps coarse inbound abuse protection only. Verify what exists in the Control Plane first.
dependencies: Control Plane entitlement for concurrency per org
durable frontier always on in production
planeOwner: Ingestion Plane + Frontend gateway + Control Plane (entitlements)
risks: Mis-set limits block onboarding crawls; keep the count in Postgres only to avoid Firecrawl's Redis-plus-Postgres reconciler drift. Do not copy Firecrawl's broker prefetch or FoundationDB backend. || Over-tight limits frustrate interactive browsing, so keep interactive and agent classes separate and the global bucket generous. || Double enforcement in gateway and Quarry if ownership is unclear; per-process buckets are inaccurate across edge replicas unless shared storage is used.

verevon.exactGap: The gateway already has a distributed token-bucket limiter (one 600 rpm class in rate_limit.rs, layered over every merged router including browser/search/ingestions and, because it runs before require_session, effectively keyed by client IP; per-org inner limiters exist only on mcp, agents_runs, eval and memory, and mail-task has its own class), so 'no rate limiting on these routes' is wrong, while Control Plane already holds plan-keyed QuotaLimits (billing-core: api_calls/users/storage_mb) and org-core org_quotas rows but no browser/crawl concurrency keys, and quarry-edge Claims carry no plan data. In Quarry the only capacity controls are a process-global RuntimeLeasePool semaphore (2 local-Chromium / 4 Browserbase permits, keyed by host, org_id empty on the internal lease), a global AutoscaledPool and a per-host AIMD HostScheduler: there is no per-org concurrency, backlog or fair share, and agent browser runs (ChromiumoxideDriver plus the agent_runs map) have no cap at all. The Postgres queue is a per-crawl frontier (pop is scoped to org_id + queue_id and the queue name derives from the run id), so a cross-job org backlog cannot live there; the real admission seam is the quarry-control jobs table that the orchestrator dispatcher polls.

verevon.constraints: Control Plane owns the numbers (org_quota.rs quotes CLAUDE.md: quotas and entitlements live in Control Plane), Quarry only enforces; no cross-plane DB reads, so Quarry needs an org-core read through a service credential, which requires a new row in cross-plane-token-requests.json plus a registry grant (none exists for org-core), or auth-core must mint limits into the token (Claims has no such field). Model proposes / Quarry executes: agent browser runs are started by execution-core through the broker grant, so the cap belongs at Quarry StartRun and must return a typed retryable 429 that execution-core treats as backpressure, not as a failed task. ZDR: backlog or admission rows must not persist URLs or payloads for ZDR requests (counts or in-memory only). The gateway allowlist in orgs/quotas.rs forbids adding a quota key before something reads it, so key, reader and UI land in one change.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Correct the premise (the gateway already rate-limits every route with one IP-keyed class) and split the work: (a) gateway: add class-aware, org-keyed inner limiters for browser, scrape/search and agent classes using the existing mcp.rs pattern, keeping interactive and agent classes separate (S); (b) Quarry: per-org permits at RuntimeLeasePool and a cap on agent_runs plus agent sessions, which first requires threading org_id into the adapter acquire (it is empty today) (M); (c) job backlog and fair share belong at the quarry-control jobs / orchestrator dispatcher, not in postgres_queue.rs, whose queues are per crawl run (M); (d) numbers come from new org-core org_quotas keys read via a service credential with an explicit fail-open or fail-closed decision, plus billing-core plan defaults. Drop the 'claims carry plan limits' variant unless auth-core is changed.
verevon.effortNote: Original M covers only one plane. Gateway classes are S, Quarry per-org permits M, job admission with backlog M, Control Plane keys plus manifest grant S-M; also needs an ADR for fail-open vs fail-closed.
verevon.verdictReason: The need is real (no per-org capacity in Quarry, agent runs uncapped) but the item misstates the gateway (a global limiter exists), misplaces the backlog in a per-crawl frontier queue, and understates the cross-plane work.

title: Per-operation browser deadlines, bounded tab attach and retry-once on a destroyed execution context
summary: Give every CDP operation in quarry-browser an explicit deadline from one constants table (command, page-ready, capture, accessibility quiet window, tab attach), wrapped by a single helper that returns a typed Timeout with the operation name. Add one retry for lightweight calls that fail with a destroyed execution context (re-resolving the context first), and never replay coordinate actions after state changed. Make the table overridable per run policy.
whyItMatters: Hung or flaky browser steps are the first thing users watching the live view and agents will notice, and they waste Model steps on transport errors. The fix is small and has a clear reference design.

others: Firecrawl AbortManager (SRC) and Crawlee handler timeout (DOC) bound whole requests rather than each operation
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources has a per-operation table (Codex); every reference bounds work in some form, so the capability is common even though the table is unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A constants table of deadlines wrapped around every CDP call (about 20 s per command, 15 s page-ready, 1.5 s cursor, 5 s capture, 750 ms accessibility quiet cap), with debugger leases cleaned up on timeout. A pending-open map resolves when a tab attaches or rejects after a 15 s handshake with distinct failure causes. DOM operations cache an isolated world per (target, frame, loader); on a context-destroyed error the cache is dropped and the call is retried once. Semantic errors are never retried.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: Only download begin/complete (10 s / 30 s), snapshot capture (5 s) and a few bounded waits carry explicit timeouts. The BrowserConfig builder sets no request or launch timeout, so CDP calls rely on the chromiumoxide library default (not verified). Agent runs are bounded only by step and runtime budgets (max_steps 12, max_runtime_s 120 in the gateway request). No documented retry-once rule exists for destroyed contexts or stale targets, although stale nodes already fail instead of being rebound (chromiumoxide.rs:2116).

approachOriginal: Ingestion Plane (quarry-browser): add a deadlines module and a cdp_call(op, fut) helper using tokio::time::timeout, returning ErrorCode::Timeout with details {op, ms}; wrap navigation, evaluate, screenshot, accessibility snapshot, input dispatch and tab/target attach. Add a retry_once_on_context_destroyed helper for DOM evaluation and snapshot calls only. Surface stale targets as TargetRepairRequired where appropriate and count timeouts in metrics. Calibrate values against Verevon's own latency histograms instead of copying Codex's numbers, and make them overridable through the run constraints. Model Plane: add the planner rule 'retry a lightweight call once after a short wait; never replay coordinates after the page changed'.
dependencies: Optional: F-t2-047 typed sub-codes for the timeout detail
planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (quarry-browser); Model Plane for the planner rule
risks: Deadlines that are too tight cause false failures on slow pages, so make them configurable and log which operation timed out.

verevon.exactGap: Explicit deadlines exist only for download begin and complete (10 s and 30 s, chromiumoxide.rs:76-77), the 5 s profile-capture wrapper (683-693), caller-bounded waits (1733-1740, 2807) and lease acquisition (lease_pool.rs:124); everything else (navigate, content, evaluate, screenshot, AX snapshot, input, tab open) rides chromiumoxide's library default request_timeout of 30 s because the BrowserConfig builder sets none (226-262; chromiumoxide-0.9.1 handler/mod.rs:34, 681), and failures surface as DriverFailed strings rather than a typed Timeout naming the operation (1988-2004, 2017-2023) while DriverFailed is not retryable (error.rs:38-43). Quarry already fails stale or destroyed-frame ref targets with TargetRepairRequired 'observe again' instead of rebinding (1245-1278, 2100-2140), and the Model Plane already retries transient failures of non-risky tool calls up to three times (runtime_loop/retry.rs:37) but deliberately never retries browser.act or browser_agent (permission/mod.rs:261-271). Agent runs are bounded by max_steps and max_runtime_s only (gateway sets 12 and 120, browser.rs:483-490; agent_routes.rs:446-451).
reuse: ErrorCode::Timeout (retryable, HTTP 504) and ErrorCode::TargetRepairRequired already in quarry-core
BrowserConfig builder request_timeout and launch_timeout setters (library supports them)
BrowserTelemetry startup_latency_ms and the lease pool metrics for calibrating values
Existing hydration settle budget and wait_for timeouts in BrowserDriverAdapter
AgentConstraints (max_runtime_s) as the vehicle for per-run overrides
verevon.constraints: Deadlines are Quarry execution policy: per-run overrides may only tighten or stay under a Quarry-side maximum, the Model must not be able to widen them (Model proposes, Quarry executes). Retrying actions is unsafe by design: the Model Plane gates browser.act and browser_agent as risky and the retry helper is risk-gated for the same reason (retry.rs:1-25), and ref-bound actions already fail closed with TargetRepairRequired. ZDR is unaffected; timeouts must not log URLs or page text into details under ZDR.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Keep it inside quarry-browser, S in size. Set request_timeout and launch_timeout explicitly on the BrowserConfig builder, add a small deadlines module with one cdp_call(op, fut) wrapper that returns ErrorCode::Timeout with details {op, ms} (and wrap goto, which today maps any failure to DriverFailed), and add retry-once only for idempotent read calls (content, AX snapshot, evaluate) when the error text indicates a destroyed context. Never retry ref or coordinate actions; they keep surfacing TargetRepairRequired. Drop the proposed Model Plane planner rule: Model Plane already retries non-risky transient failures, and browser actions are intentionally excluded. Calibrate deadlines from telemetry rather than copying Codex's numbers. Note the item's evidence line chromiumoxide.rs:685 is the profile-capture timeout, not an accessibility snapshot, and there is no 750 ms AX quiet-window equivalent in Quarry.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged. The Model Plane half of the item disappears, and the library already supplies a 30 s per-command floor.
verevon.verdictReason: Partial is right and the quick-win size holds, but the Model Plane planner rule conflicts with the risk-gated retry design, the evidence line for the accessibility timeout is wrong, and the item missed that the library already enforces a 30 s per-command timeout and that DriverFailed is non-retryable. Reword to a quarry-browser-only change.

title: Honest bot-block handling: closed block taxonomy, non-signals, one recovery, a user-visible blocked state, and no stealth code
summary: Split outcomes into strong bot-block signals (captcha, WAF interstitial, challenge loop) and non-signals (bare 403/429, timeouts, sign-in or paywall pages, region blocks). Add a closed BlockReason enum with hostname-only aggregated telemetry, give the browser planner an explicit rule (at most one low-risk recovery such as a short wait and one reload, then stop, tell the user and switch source), and render a 'site blocked automated access' state with take-over and try-another-source actions in the Verevon browser. Delete the unused stealth scripts and the vestigial stealth_level plumbing.
whyItMatters: Users and agents get a truthful, consistent result when a site blocks automation, and enterprise buyers get a defensible no-evasion posture that fits 'Model proposes, Quarry executes or rejects'. Hostname-only counters are ZDR-safe and can feed the later domain registry. The dead stealth code currently contradicts the stance.

others: Apify academy (DOC): detection taxonomy, but it recommends evasion, so only the taxonomy is useful
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 4 sources (Codex, Apify); differentiator, and the one that matches Verevon's governance stance
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A classifier reads site-served evidence (URL, DOM markers of Cloudflare/Akamai/hCaptcha/Turnstile, a fresh screenshot) and outputs {kind, confidence, evidence}. Strong signals versus non-signals are defined explicitly: bare 403/429, timeouts, sign-in pages, paywalls and region blocks are not bot detection. At most one recovery (short wait, single reload), no fingerprint or network changes, then stop and tell the user. A closed-reason report (captcha_failed, access_denied, challenge_loop, unexpected_bot_error) records only the hostname.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: Detection exists: ChallengeKind (Captcha/Waf/Login/Consent/RateLimit/AccessDenied/Unknown), ChallengeSignal.requires_escalation defaulting to true, ErrorCode::ChallengeDetected. Missing: explicit non-signal rules (the host scheduler lumps 401/403/451/999/CDN-challenge into one Blocked bucket), a closed report taxonomy with hostname-only telemetry, planner text for the one-recovery rule, and a user-facing blocked state. stealth.rs (STEALTH_SCRIPT and an auto-accept CONSENT_DISMISS_SCRIPT) has no caller outside its own file, and DriverPlan.stealth_level is set (0/1/2) but never read outside driver_plan.rs, so the code contradicts the stance and one baseline narrative wrongly describes it as active.

approachOriginal: Ingestion Plane: add a BlockReason closed enum (strong: captcha, waf_challenge, challenge_loop; non-signal reasons stay as rate_limited, auth_required, paywall, geo_blocked), reusing the taxonomies already proposed in SOVEREIGN_SCRAPING_RELIABILITY.md section 4 and the improvements doc section 39, plus a hostname-only counter (no URL, path or content; in-memory count only for ZDR orgs). Split the host scheduler's Blocked bucket so a bare 403 is not auto-classified as a bot block. Model Plane: add the strong-signal / non-signal and one-recovery rule to the browser planner instructions, mapped onto ChallengeSignal (locate the planner prompt in the Model Plane first). Frontend Plane: show a 'Site blocked automated access' state in the browser pane with 'Take over' and 'Try another source' actions. Delete stealth.rs and stealth_level. If a consent helper is ever wired it should default to declining non-essential cookies or asking the user, never accepting on their behalf (INF).
planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (taxonomy, telemetry, dead-code removal); Model Plane (planner rule); Frontend Plane (UI state)
risks: Misreading a transient 403 as a bot block could end runs early, so keep confidence thresholds and the single-retry rule. The later egress-tier work (R-t2-04-07) must not use proxy rotation to escape a strong signal.

alreadyPlanned.where: [R-t2-04-03] Partly: docs/SOVEREIGN_SCRAPING_RELIABILITY.md section 4 plans a challenge classifier with reasons (bot_wall, captcha, auth_required, paywall, geo_blocked, robots_disallowed) and QUARRY_V2_BROWSER_AUTOMATION_IMPROVEMENTS_2026_OWNERSHIP_RECONCILED.md section 39 plans an acquisition-failure taxonomy; neither specifies non-signals, the one-recovery rule, hostname-only telemetry or the UI state

verevon.exactGap: SRC: detection exists but is crude and never reaches the planner or UI: observation.rs:158-213 substring-matches url/title/text ('sign in', 'forbidden', 'cookie consent', 'access denied') and emits ChallengeSignal with a fixed 0.98 confidence and requires_escalation=true for every hit, so ordinary login and consent pages count as challenges, while execution-core's BrowserObservation (browser_agent.rs:171-186) and both planner prompts (llm_planner.rs:236-244; model-gateway http_routes.rs:2013-2022, which only forbids CAPTCHA solving and anti-bot bypass) never see the signal and BrowserChrome has a takeover chip (BrowserChrome.tsx:1228-1236) but no blocked state. SRC: the only user-facing blocked text is the gateway's classify_scrape_failure (knowledge/quarry.rs:287-294), which labels any 403/429 'site_blocked' and suggests asking for proxy access, and host_scheduler.rs:36-47 lumps 401/403/451/999/CDN-challenge into one Blocked bucket mapped from ErrorCode::Forbidden/UpstreamBlocked (pipeline.rs:372-374). SRC: stealth.rs (its header says it exists to pass Cloudflare's free tier) and DriverPlan.stealth_level are dead (lib.rs:164 declares the module, nothing calls it), but live evasion-adjacent behaviour remains: TLS-impersonation escalation on prior_block_signals (driver_plan.rs:45-47), driver rotation on 401/403/407/429/503 (fallback_driver.rs:95-108; fingerprint_rotation.rs:16-18), proxy rotation after block statuses (egress_broker.rs:155-163) and a shipped 'stealth' RunPolicy preset (presets.go:84-96).
evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/observation.rs:154-214 (classify_challenge) and :898-935 (per-run challenge counts and rate)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/stealth.rs:1-12 (header intent) and crates/quarry-browser/src/lib.rs:164 (module declared, no callers)
reuse: ChallengeKind/ChallengeSignal contracts and ErrorCode::ChallengeDetected
BrowserTelemetry.challenge_observation_count and challenge_rate_per_mille (already per run, no URL)
BrowserChrome human_takeover control chip and the owner timeline as the host for the blocked state
gateway classify_scrape_failure (rewrite, do not add a second classifier)
host_scheduler BadKind and the pipeline error mapping for the Blocked split
verevon.constraints: Model proposes / Quarry executes or rejects: the one-recovery rule must be enforced in Quarry (stop returning actions or return ChallengeDetected after N challenge observations, using the existing per-run counter) and only mirrored in planner text, which is advisory. ZDR: per-run counters already carry no URL; a hostname aggregate must be in-memory only for ZDR orgs as the item says. Two separate Model Plane prompts exist (execution-core llm_planner.rs and model-gateway http_routes.rs browser-suggest), and the no-evasion stance must also cover the live TLS-impersonation, rotation and preset paths or it will contradict shipped behaviour.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reorder the work: (1) add the challenge signal to execution-core BrowserObservation and the planner observation text first, otherwise a planner rule has nothing to key on; (2) replace the substring classifier with tiered evidence (strong: captcha widget or WAF interstitial markers and repeated challenge across steps; non-signals: login, consent, bare 403/429, paywall, region) and stop defaulting requires_escalation=true; (3) enforce the single recovery in Quarry; (4) rewrite classify_scrape_failure; (5) make an explicit decision on the live paths (TLS-impersonation escalation, block-status driver and proxy rotation, the 'stealth' preset: rename or remove) alongside deleting stealth.rs and stealth_level; (6) build the blocked state on the existing takeover control.
verevon.effortNote: S understates it: classifier rewrite in Quarry, signal plumbing plus prompt rule in the Model Plane, a UI state in the Frontend Plane and scheduler/gateway fixes span four components; the dead-code deletion alone is S.
verevon.verdictReason: Detection and a takeover control exist, but the signal never reaches the planner or UI, the current classifier and gateway text contradict the proposed non-signal rules, and the live evasion-adjacent paths are broader than the dead stealth module the item targets.

title: Page context to chat: Quarry hit-test, @tab mentions, selection and region attachments, frame context menu
summary: Add a Quarry hit-test endpoint that turns a frame point or region into an element descriptor (AX ref, role, name, nearby text, bbox, crop, tab id, URL, snapshot generation). Build the SPA side: a select mode in BrowserChrome, region and image attachments, and an @tab mention token {sessionId, tabId, title, url, snapshotGeneration} that the gateway re-validates against Quarry fail-closed before use. Attachments are labelled 'from page' for the user before sending and enter the Model as BrowserScraped provenance (screened). A right-click menu over the frame (Ask, Explain, Summarize page, Send to Knowledge, Open in new tab) reuses the same hit-test. || Add a mention token for a live browser session or tab (for example verevon://browser-session/<id>/tab/<id>?title&url) to the chat composer. Model Plane resolves it server-side through a Quarry session ownership check on org and actor, validates the title and URL against the live tab, and never treats the mention as a grant.
whyItMatters: Point at the thing and ask about it is the highest-leverage way for the user and the agent to share a browser, and the element descriptors map straight onto the AX refs that browser.act already uses. It also unblocks on-page annotation (R-t2-08-11). || Lets users point the agent at the exact page they are looking at in the in-app browser. Small UX win.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Mention token tab-v1 {browserId, tabId, title, url}; on use list the tabs and require an exact match or report 'unavailable'. Selection payload {text | region{elementSummary, previewImage, elements[{selector, tagName, role, text, alt, src, href}]}}, kept per tab and cleared on navigation. Codex also shows page-provided metadata or suggested prompts to the user, labelled, and the model only gets what the user submits. For Verevon: BrowserChrome select mode, the gateway asks Quarry to hit-test the frame point, Quarry returns an AX-ref descriptor plus crop, attached to chat with {sessionId, tabId, url, snapshot generation} and re-validated before any action. || Merged items add: The mention carries browserId, tabId, title and url; the resolver selects the matching browser or profile and checks that the snapshot title and URL still match the live tab before use.

title: Quarry /metrics recorder, per-run statistics and graceful drain, then a span vocabulary, memory-aware admission and alert rules
summary: Phase 1 (S, ship first): install the metrics-exporter-prometheus recorder in quarry-edge, serve /metrics on an internal-only port with about 20 low-cardinality series (queue depth, browser pool active/idle/launch latency, driver outcome by driver and outcome, egress broker health, cache hit/miss, webhook delivery), and persist a RunStatistics object on the run row (finished/failed/retried, retry histogram, status-code counts, top error signatures). Phase 2: infrastructure alert rules on the existing Control Plane Prometheus, plus user-facing run-failure and data-quality alert rules in quarry-control delivered through notification-core. Phase 3, after item 01: a span vocabulary (browser.<action> with url.origin, driver, outcome, snapshot bytes; scrape.pipeline with engine attempted/winner and cache state) with approval wait excluded from agent latency, and W3C traceparent propagation gateway to execution-core to Quarry. || Install a Prometheus recorder and serve /metrics on quarry-edge with low-cardinality queue depth, lease pool, per-org active runs and step latency; add SIGTERM drain to edge and the orchestrator worker. Then wrap the browser lease pool with the existing AutoscaledPool driven by cgroup memory and Chromium RSS, refusing leases above a threshold with a typed RESOURCE_BUSY the Model Plane can retry, and report the host unhealthy after repeated refusals.
whyItMatters: Quarry has no metrics, so there are no SLOs, capacity planning or alerts for the browser and crawl layer that users and agents depend on, and scheduled monitors can break silently. Latency attribution across gateway, Model and Quarry is how slow or failing agent runs get debugged. || Autoscaling, admission and the reaper all need real numbers. referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Recorder at startup and an internal /metrics route; counters labelled by driver and outcome, never by URL or org id. Admission refuses to lease a job when CPU or memory exceeds 0.8, and after 25 consecutive refusals marks the worker unhealthy so it stops receiving work. Each process serves /health (1 s timeout) and /metrics, renews job locks on a timer and, on SIGTERM, stops claiming and finishes active jobs.

title: Monitor change quality: normalised-content fingerprint, text/JSON diffs, tags and an optional goal-aware judge
summary: Phase 1 (priority): compare a fingerprint of normalised main-content markdown instead of the raw response bytes, return a paragraph diff from /v1/change/check using the unused diff_paragraphs, accept a tag so one URL can keep separate histories, and add an optional schema-based JSON diff. Phase 2 (recommended, needs the model grant): a Model Plane judge reads the diff and the monitor's stated goal and returns {meaningful, confidence, reason, changes[]}; alerts fire when meaningful or when the judge fails (fail open).
whyItMatters: Monitoring already ships in the Verevon UI, so noise (ads, timestamps flagged as change) and the absence of any diff are visible to users now. A goal-aware verdict turns monitors into an agent-grade feature and cuts notification noise in the Application Plane.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Store the last snapshot per (org, url, tag). Normalise before compare (strip whitespace, iframe links, volatile tokens); status new|same|changed|removed from presence and equality; on changed produce a unified diff (similar crate) and, when a schema is given, extract JSON on both sides and diff fields. Judge: prompt = goal + optional extraction prompt + unified diff + field diffs; temperature 0, 30 s timeout, 3 retries with jitter, strict JSON {meaningful, confidence, reason, changes[]}; persist the verdict with the diff artifact; alert when meaningful or when judging fails.

title: Tenant-scoped, SSRF-guarded outbound webhooks with per-job events, then completion-triggered follow-ups and generalised monitors
summary: Keep the quarry-control dispatcher (HMAC signing, 1s/5s/30s/5m/1h backoff, DLQ, retry route; stronger than Firecrawl's single attempt) and add org_id on webhook registrations, edge exposure, per-job webhook config with event filters and metadata echo, and an SSRF-guarded client (port the Model Plane safe_mcp_http_client rules; the dispatcher uses a plain http.Client, INF). title: Durable hosted browser sessions: idle and absolute TTLs, suspend/resume, view vs control tokens, optional recording, scrape-to-session replay
summary: Move agent browser run state from the in-process run map to a durable session store with a state machine (starting, running, suspended, stopped, failed), idempotent create, separate idle and absolute TTLs instead of the fixed 120 s / 12 step UI defaults, and suspend/resume implemented as a profile snapshot plus browser release and restore. Issue separate read-only and interactive live-view tokens and add optional recording gated by org policy (off under ZDR). As a later phase, persist a ReplayContext (url, actions, profile, location) on scrape results and add POST /v1/scrape/:id/session so a user or a Model run can continue from a scrape result.
whyItMatters: Two minutes is short for real browsing, an in-process map loses runs on restart, and enterprises want audit recordings. The plan documents say crash-safe resume is not yet proven for every provider, and 'continue interactively from this scrape' is a natural AI-first flow.

others: Apify container URL and live view exposing DevTools (apify-platform-061, DOC)
Firecrawl scrape-to-interact replay (firecrawl-engine-and-infra-021, SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Session lifecycle and live view: 2 of 4 sources (firecrawl, apify), differentiator. Replay: 1 of 4, unique.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Session row {state, created_at, last_activity_at, idle_ttl, abs_ttl, idempotency_key}; create is idempotent via Idempotency-Key with retries, long-poll until running; a reaper transitions rows on TTL; suspend = snapshot profile and release the browser, resume = new browser plus restore; live view = signed short-lived URLs with view and control scopes; recording = screencast frames to segmented video, disabled under ZDR. Replay: store {url, waitFor, actions, profile, location} with each scrape; promote(scrape_id) verifies the caller owns it, creates a session, replays, and hands the session id to the agent or UI.

title: Durable, tenant-scoped authority and one audit record for every permission and approval decision
summary: Persist BrowserBroker grants (today an in-memory map), add a production issuance path and scope inheritance for child runs and fleets, and put evaluate and raw-CSS actions behind a sensitive one-shot grant. Add org_id to the quarry-control Webhook model, front webhook CRUD through edge with JWT org scoping, and add a dispatch-id header, a test endpoint and a longer retry ladder. Define an AuthzDecision event in audit-core (schema_version, permission, decision, decision_context, a decided_by enum separating user, saved, policy, reviewer and system, policy_id, reason_code, origin only, run_id, actor_id, duration_ms) that execution-core approvals, browser-broker validations and Quarry policy denials publish to verevon.audit.v2.*; record only denials for high-volume per-navigation checks.
whyItMatters: It keeps the authority model credible (Quarry executes only what a grant allows and scope cannot widen through child runs or webhooks) and completes the evidence chain for "the Model proposes, Quarry executes or rejects", which enterprise compliance reviews ask for. Without tenant-scoped webhooks, crawl and monitor webhooks cannot be exposed to customers.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex (one structured record per permission decision with decided_by, decision_context, origin only and duration_ms, denials-only for URL checks; Allow/Prompt/Forbidden policy vocabulary) and Apify (limited-permission default with scoped, expiring tokens inherited by runs and webhooks)
others: Aside (read methods whitelisted; lifecycle mutations only through ownership-tracking tools)
Apify webhooks (11 retries over about 32 hours, dispatch-id header, test button, no HMAC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Least-privilege permissions 3 of 4 (table-stakes); decision audit record 1 of 4 (Codex, unique); webhook reliability 1 of 4 (Apify, DOC)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Grant = {principal, scopes[], allowed_domains[], budget, expires_at, parent_grant}; children inherit min(parent scopes) and escalation needs a recorded human approval. The component that decides emits AuthzDecision with an outcome enum {not_needed, policy_allowed, reviewer_approved, reviewer_denied, user_approved, user_approved_for_session, user_denied, user_aborted, timeout}. Webhooks are (org_id, url, secret, events), HMAC signed, retried with exponential backoff, DLQ at the end, registered only through edge.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: Grants are validated before every action (15 minute TTL, host allowlist, org and owner scope) and sensitive one-shot grants exist, but the store is a mutex-guarded in-memory map and no production path issues grants, so history is lost on restart. The sensitive-action allowlist is only respond_dialog, upload_ref and download_ref, so evaluate and raw-CSS run on an ordinary grant (unless the Model Plane risk gate separately prompts; not verified here). The Webhook struct has no OrgID and the routes are not exposed through edge; delivery is HMAC signed with 5 attempts then a DLQ. Browser approvals record (decision, decided_by, reason) and tool_action audit events carry ZDR tags, but there is no cross-plane schema, no decided_by enum, no duration, and grant validations and Quarry policy denials do not reach audit-core.

verevon.constraints: Plane ownership: grants belong to the Model Plane (browser-broker, Go with no database today, so durable storage adds a datastore dependency); Quarry only validates. No cross-plane DB access: Quarry must publish AuthzDecision over NATS and never write audit-core tables, and because Quarry has no audit publisher one must be added with its own plane/producer/event subject family and publish grant (audit-core rejects an event whose subject tokens do not match the payload). Privacy and ZDR: events carry origin only and ZDR tags, never full URLs, and per-navigation validations should be recorded denials-only. Space authority: child-run and fleet grants may only narrow (min of parent scopes) and never inherit wider authority through a Space. The webhook org_id migration must handle existing unscoped rows fail-closed.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split into three independently shippable items. (a) Durable, issued BrowserBroker grants, merged with F-t2-001 rather than treating persistence and issuance separately, with parent/child inheritance on the existing parent_grant_id binding. (b) Quarry webhook tenant scoping: org_id column with migration, edge-fronted org-scoped CRUD, dispatch-id header. (c) AuthzDecision audit as a new event name on the existing verevon.audit.v2 flat shape, first published by session-core/execution-core approval decisions with decided_by filled from the durable record, and only later by Quarry policy denials. Demote the evaluate/raw-CSS sensitive-allowlist change to low-priority hardening because both facades already refuse those actions.
verevon.effortNote: As one item this bundles a new broker datastore plus issuance path, a Quarry webhook migration and edge exposure, and a cross-plane audit event with a new Quarry publisher. Split, it is roughly M (webhooks), M (audit) and L (durable grants plus issuance, overlapping F-t2-001).
